overall_reason: A share dialog that mixes two alignment axes: the title, the document chip and the access row are centred, while the 'Copy link' button sits right-aligned in a footer.

score.reason: T-SQUINT reads the dark 'Copy link' button first and the centred rows above as one pale stack, and T-LEFT-EDGES finds no shared left edge: text starts at x=504, 518 and 448 on three rows.

findings.where: title, document chip and permission row against the footer button, 1440 and 375
findings.evidence: In dom-1440.json the card spans x=397 to 679 (centre 538). 'Share handoff' (x=504, 68px), 'Launch brief' (x=518, 60px) and the access row (x=448 to 628) are each centred on 538, while 'Copy link' (x=580, 87px) is right-aligned. 01-evidence/tiles/1440-00.png shows three centred lines over a right-aligned action.
findings.before: Three centred rows and one right-aligned action: two axes in a 282px card.
findings.after: Put the dialog on one axis: left-align the title, document and access row on the card's inner edge, and keep the action right in the footer as a dialog convention.
findings.why: Centred short lines give the eye no start edge, and the move from centre to right makes the action look detached from the settings it applies.

strengths: The single filled action, 'Copy link', is the heaviest block and sits where dialog actions are expected.
